input.source_text: [s1] The neighborhood council trained its own water technicians. [s2] The supplier alone can unlock the meter needed to restore service. [s3] Technical competence therefore leaves restoration dependent on the supplier until another access route exists.

expected_governing_concept_alternatives: Competence does not end dependence while an indispensable gate remains externally controlled.
required_relations: Restoration requires unlocking; supplier alone controls unlocking.
conditions_to_preserve: An alternative access route could change the relation.
undergeneralization_traps: Reducing the relation to water management.
acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent wording that preserves the causal relation and its limits is acceptable.

input.source_text: [s1] Mira can diagnose the pump alone, but only her mentor holds the workshop key. [s2] Each repair still requires his approval to enter. [s3] Her growing skill has not yet given her control of access.

expected_governing_concept_alternatives: Capability without control of a required resource leaves dependence intact.
required_relations: Repair requires access; mentor controls access; skill does not remove that gate.
conditions_to_preserve: Dependence concerns workshop access, not all decisions.
undergeneralization_traps: Retelling Mira and the pump without the access relation.
acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent wording that preserves the causal relation and its limits is acceptable.

input.source_text: [s1] The River Party promised its ally a vote on the harbor bill. [s2] Later it gained enough seats to pass the bill alone. [s3] Its chair said the promise still governed the vote even though the ally’s seats were no longer necessary. [s4] The account establishes a stated commitment, not proof that the promise will be kept.

expected_governing_concept_alternatives: Removal of instrumental dependence does not by itself extinguish a stated commitment.
required_relations: Seat dependence ends; stated promise remains a separate reason for conduct.
conditions_to_preserve: The chair states a position; future compliance is unverified.
overgeneralization_traps: All political promises survive every change.
The party actually kept its promise.
undergeneralization_traps: Treating this as continuing dependence on the ally’s seats.
Calling it politics without the changed necessity relation.
acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent wording that preserves the causal relation and its limits is acceptable.

input.source_text: [s1] Neri now has her own workshop key and can perform every repair alone. [s2] She still asks her former mentor to attend because she promised to teach his replacement alongside him. [s3] His presence is no longer required for access; the continuing request follows their stated commitment.

expected_governing_concept_alternatives: Continuing collaboration may follow commitment after access dependence has ended.
required_relations: Independent access removes the old gate; a promise explains continued requests.
conditions_to_preserve: The passage supplies a reason for this request, not a universal theory of loyalty.
undergeneralization_traps: Retelling keys and mentorship without distinguishing commitment from necessity.
acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent wording that preserves the causal relation and its limits is acceptable.

input.source_text: [s1] A rehearsal restored every sample record correctly. [s2] The owner authorized rehearsal only and reserved approval of the live migration. [s3] The successful test supplies evidence of readiness, not permission to migrate.

expected_governing_concept_alternatives: Evidence of capability and authority to act are distinct conditions.
required_relations: Rehearsal success supports readiness; live action still requires separate approval.
conditions_to_preserve: Authorization is explicitly limited to rehearsal.
undergeneralization_traps: Listing test steps while omitting the separate approval gate.
acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent wording that preserves the causal relation and its limits is acceptable.

input.source_text: [s1] At the closed rehearsal, listeners laughed at Elin’s story about her brother. [s2] He had allowed the rehearsal but had not agreed to its use at the public memorial. [s3] The warm response changed Elin’s confidence, not the scope of his consent.

expected_governing_concept_alternatives: Audience response can support confidence without expanding the permission granted.
required_relations: Warm response affects confidence; consent remains scoped to rehearsal.
conditions_to_preserve: Different audience and occasion; brother’s consent is unresolved for the memorial.
undergeneralization_traps: Calling this grief alone while losing the response/permission distinction.
acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent wording that preserves the causal relation and its limits is acceptable.

input.task: Construct a new strategic article using the supplied analytical framework where the facts support it. Transfer relationships, not donor wording or historical facts. The subject is fictional.
input.source_text: [f1] Alder financed shared river-energy infrastructure for Bell and Rook. [f2] Bell can now fund its own upgrades but the old board still gives Alder approval over every project. [f3] Rook remains dependent on shared maintenance crews and fears service interruptions. [f4] A technically viable new grid plan does not settle how the three partners share approval authority. [f5] Bell requests more autonomy; Alder wants predictable joint operating standards. [f6] None of the partners has announced withdrawal. [f7] Future trust, investment and institutional outcomes are unknown.

style_operator_findings.definition: Reject reliance on time, succession, trade, or historical evolution to solve political problems automatically.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Use to expose abdication of agency, not to dismiss all gradualism.

style_operator_findings.definition: Compress the final lesson into a balanced general principle after sustained analysis.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Compression follows complexity; it should not substitute for evidence.

style_operator_findings.definition: Delay prescription until the diagnostic structure has been established, then offer bounded proposals with caveats.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Avoid premature solutioneering; proposal must be earned by prior analysis.

style_operator_findings.definition: Contrast technical management of existing facts with statesmanlike creation of future political reality.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Must be supported by article-level development; otherwise it becomes empty grandiosity.

style_operator_findings.definition: Begin from a shared institutional aspiration before introducing difficulty.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Reuse the move from shared aspiration to sober diagnosis, not source phrasing.

style_operator_findings.definition: Argue that an irreversible development should be guided rather than obstructed.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Require evidence of structural inevitability before invoking.

style_operator_findings.definition: Show that a successful policy created the new difficulty it must now manage.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Use for second-order consequences of success, not generic unintended consequences.

style_operator_findings.definition: Turn apparent progress into the reason hidden obstacles must be faced.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Preserve the inversion from success to difficulty without copying the article's examples.

style_operator_findings.definition: Reconstruct multiple actors' positions through their obligations, history, geography, power, and fears.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Do not flatten all actors into equal truth; preserve asymmetry and judgment.

style_operator_findings.definition: Recast technical, territorial, or institutional issues as questions of confidence, vulnerability, self-esteem, or will.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Use psychological meaning only when source evidence supports actor vulnerability or confidence pressure.

style_operator_findings.definition: Treat local controversies as symptoms of a deeper structural reality.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Use for diagnosis of systems where symptoms hide deeper regime change.

style_operator_findings.definition: Show that a technically correct answer can fail because the real problem is political acceptance and legitimacy.
style_operator_findings.transfer_boundary: Technical detail must remain visible; do not replace it with vague psychology.

attractor_routes.notes: Full article-level argument craft route from aspiration to creative-realism close.
Closing movement from passive optimism to creative political reality.
Converts visible controversy into actor-bound structural diagnosis.
Moves from technical adequacy to political meaning and constructive channeling.

input.target: Write four to six paragraphs for a general reader. Preserve the different constraints of Alder, Bell and Rook. Diagnose before proposing conditional changes. Do not force an inevitability claim or guaranteed outcome. No internal operator IDs, scoring instructions or source-era actors belong in the public article.

required_relations: Successful assistance enables Bell autonomy without establishing Rook independence.
Technical feasibility does not establish legitimacy of approval arrangements.
Proposals must be conditional and responsive to asymmetric interests.
overgeneralization_traps: Withdrawal or trust restoration asserted as fact
generation_checks: An earned multi-paragraph argument, not an operator list
No imported source-era facts or unsupported real-world news
acceptable_alternatives: Several conditional governance or consultation proposals can fit the bounded facts.
